01 / Core abstractions

Core abstractions

Eight concepts describe the entities, state, possibilities, actions, processes, and changes in an interactive world. Open a row for its definition and example.

01Worldthe current state of everything
What it is

The container for current entities, relationships, registered actions, and ordered events.

Exampleworld.snapshot()
→ entities + relationships + actions
Source ↗
02Entitya stable identity for one thing
What it is

An ID, label, type, and component map. The entity is intentionally light; its components carry meaning.

Examplerobot_01
type: core.robot
Source ↗
03Componentstate or ability attached to an entity
What it is

A composable piece of state or capability such as locomotion, transform, observable, power, vision, or audio.

Examplerobot_01.components.locomotion
→ { state: "ready" }
Source ↗
04Relationshipa directed fact connecting two entities
What it is

A first-class subject–predicate–object connection, with optional metadata.

Examplerobot_01 — located_in — world_local
robot_01 — observes — world_local
Source ↗
05Affordancewhat is possible right now
What it is

An action currently available to an actor and optional target, including the reason when it is unavailable.

Exampleworld.affordancesFor("robot_01")
→ connect · observe · map · stop
Source ↗
06Actiona meaningful operation that changes the world
What it is

An operation with actor and target requirements. It can update components, create relationships, return a result, and emit events.

Exampleworld.execute({
action_id: "world.map"
})
Source ↗
07Systema process that keeps the world moving
What it is

A continuous process that senses, updates, executes, or emits events. Systems connect the model to time and external reality.

Examplesense → update → execute
→ emit → repeat
Design notes ↗
08Eventan ordered record of a world change
What it is

A sequence-numbered record with a timestamp, type, involved entities, and event data.

Exampleaction.started
world.mapping_enabled
action.completed
Source ↗
02 / Architecture

Architecture

Adapters translate physical or simulated systems into the same world model. An optional governance path surrounds action execution when authorization and control-plane guarantees are required.

active pathLive Go2 world
Go2 sensors→standard robot port→robot-world adapter→World Runtime→operator panel
optional pathGovernance
Mission API→Mission Server→signed Authorization→Supervisor Kernel→Driver

Event Log is the cross-cutting record. Scene, Attention, Replay, and Reports are projections over it. The governance packages are retained as an optional extension; the World Runtime does not depend on them.

03 / Service contracts

Service contracts

The NEM suite defines the boundaries between clients, policy, control, hardware, capabilities, projections, and attention. Open a contract for its surface and guarantees.

01Mission APIthe single client-facing HTTP+JSON boundary
Contract

The cockpit, CLI, and agent use the same API. The server authenticates the principal, projects grants, validates requests, and owns all authority.

SurfacePOST /missions · GET /missions/{id}
POST /runs · GET /runs/{id}
POST /runs/{id}/approve|reject
GET /scene · GET /entities/{id}
Rules

Mutations accept idempotency keys. Every physical-consequence event carries a run ID. Stop is available to any principal and is never queued.

02Event Logappend-only source of truth and replay substrate
Contract

append(event) assigns a monotonic sequence and timestamp before returning. read filters by mission, run, robot, theme, or time; tail is the server-push stream.

Envelopeseq · schema_version · source
event_type · severity · timestamp
robot_id? · mission_id? · run_id?
refs[] · payload
Guarantees

Events are immutable, durable before acknowledgment, and replayable. Scene, Attention, Replay, and Reports are rebuildable projections over this log.

03Authorizationthe only artifact that can cause physical action
Contract

A signed, single-use artifact binds one run to one robot, grant, target snapshot, capability, streams, abort triggers, checks, and expiry.

Shapeauth_id · run_id · mission_id · robot_id
grant: stream | discrete
enforcement · target · streams_granted
abort_triggers · checks · signature
Lifecycle

issued → dispatched → accepted → active → completed, with terminal aborted, stopped, rejected, or expired. Persist before dispatch.

04Supervisor Kernelthe hard control-plane boundary
ContractGET /status
POST /stop
POST /execute
WS /events
Data path

Capability hosts send ActionChunks. The kernel validates the active authorization, clamps every field per tick, forwards the applied setpoint to the driver, and emits a post-clamp acknowledgment.

Guarantees

Stop, watchdog silence, stale heartbeat, expired authorization, and upstream loss drive the driver's declared safe state without waiting on the agent or Mission Server.

05Driver SPIthe hardware adapter contract
Contractmanifest() · connect() · disconnect()
status() · set_setpoint()
execute_discrete() · command_safe_state()
open_stream() · events()
Manifest

Declares action spaces, hard caps, observables, native actions, streams, sensitivity, and safe-state facts. The Go2 driver is the active physical implementation.

Status

Returns normalized robot status: heartbeat age, battery headroom, safe-state flag, pose, faults, and optional vendor display data.

06Capability SPIsandboxed executors that turn intent into chunks
Contractdescribe() · bind() · start()
on_frame() · emit_chunk()
emit_observation() · emit_event()
abort() · stop() · terminate()
Inputs

An authorization, target, and only the streams declared by the capability manifest. Observations are evidence and enter the Event Log; they do not grant authority.

Sandbox

Read-only package, scratch space, denied network by default, declared resources, and a watchdog. Chunks must cease within one watchdog interval after stop or abort.

07Scene / World Twinbelief projection and deterministic prediction
ContractGET /scene
GET /scene?since=ssg_N
GET /entities/{id}
Scene

Perception, operator, simulator, and capability observations reduce into stable entities, affordances, freshness, provenance, robots, and hazards. Writers never assert identity directly.

Twin

A pure function of a pinned scene snapshot, ontology, label map, builder, engine, policy, and seed. The same tuple must produce the same world bit-for-bit.

08Attentionthe agent’s per-mission perceptual channel
ContractGET /missions/{id}/attention
POST /missions/{id}/drain
POST /missions/{id}/wait
Shape

A contract is pinned from the mission preset for one mission and principal: state filters, CEL wake predicate, pending budget, digest version, and predicate environment version.

Guarantees

Pre-turn drains are required. Run outcomes, aborts, operator messages, and protected-class advisories remain verbatim. Delivered digest bytes are persisted for replay.

09Policy / Registrywhere packages become eligible, never authoritative
ContractGET /registry · POST /registry
GET /registry/{package}
POST /registry/{package}/pin|enable
POST /registry/{package}/promote|demote|revoke
Package

Preset rules bind verbs to robots, principals, capability versions, arguments, limits, streams, approval, freshness, and abort triggers. Packages carry manifests, hashes, signatures, and gauntlet reports.

Rules

Registry maturity and enablement are checked live at issuance. Changes obey a tightening lattice: limits and durations narrow, sets shrink, and approval or abort requirements only strengthen.

04 / Database tables

Postgres v0 layout

The repository currently uses in-memory and file-backed reference components; no SQL migrations are checked in. This is the proposed Postgres table inventory from the storage design, with the Event Log remaining the source of truth.

01event_logappend-only source of truth
Purpose

Every state change, physical consequence, observation, policy decision, and operator action. Projections must be rebuildable from it.

Columnsseq PK · schema_version · source
event_type · severity · timestamp
robot_id? · mission_id? · run_id?
refs jsonb · payload jsonb
Indexes

seq, run_id, mission_id, robot_id, event_type, and timestamp. Sequence is immutable and never reused.

02missionsmission lifecycle and pinned policy
Purpose

Operational mission identity, lifecycle, principal, robot roster, and the preset version bound at creation.

Columnsid PK · schema_version · principal
preset_id · preset_version · robot_ids jsonb
state · created_at · completed_at
result jsonb
Links

Referenced by runs, authorizations, attention_contracts, and mission-scoped events.

03runsone proposed attempt from intent to result
Purpose

Causal chain for a proposed verb, approval, authorization, execution, rejection, abort, expiry, or terminal result.

Columnsid PK · schema_version · mission_id · robot_id
verb · args jsonb · target jsonb
reason · expected_result jsonb · proposed_by
state · approval jsonb · authorization_ids jsonb
result jsonb · created_at · updated_at
Links

Every run is joined to its events by run_id and to one or more signed authorizations.

04authorizationssigned permission for bounded physical action
Purpose

Durable copy of the signed artifact the kernel verifies before dispatch. It records what was permitted and which bounds were enforceable.

Columnsid PK · schema_version · run_id · mission_id · robot_id
grant jsonb · enforcement jsonb · target jsonb
streams_granted jsonb · abort_triggers jsonb
capability jsonb · checks jsonb
issued_at · expires_at · signature · state
Links

One authorization belongs to a run; every lifecycle transition is also an immutable event.

05anomaliesopen safety and operational issues
Purpose

Tracks an observed mismatch, safety issue, suspected cause, owner, evidence, closure criteria, and current status.

Columnsid PK · schema_version · severity
mission_id? · run_id? · capability? · driver?
expected · observed · evidence_refs jsonb
suspected_cause · owner · closure_criteria · status
Rules

Transition timestamps live in event_log. Open safety anomalies block preset widening and maturity promotion, but never block stop or abort paths.

06registry_stateorganization-owned package trust state
Purpose

Current enablement, pin, maturity, gauntlet evidence, and history for installed capability or driver packages.

Columnspackage PK · enabled · pinned
maturity · gauntlet_report
history jsonb · installed_at · updated_at
Rules

Trust lives here, not in manifests. Installed does not mean authorized; issuance checks live registry state, policy, mission, and approval.

07idempotency_recordsreplay-safe mutation results
Purpose

Returns the original response for a repeated mutation from the same principal, method, route, and key.

Columnsprincipal · idempotency_key
method · path · request_hash
response_status · response_body jsonb
created_at · expires_at
Key

Unique on (principal, idempotency_key, method, path). The stored response is the replay contract.

08scene_projection_snapshotsrebuildable compact world snapshots
Purpose

Materialized /scene snapshots for fast reads. The source remains the observation events in event_log.

Columnsscene_snapshot_id PK · source_seq
ontology_version · label_map_version
freshness_ms · robots jsonb · hazards jsonb
created_at
Links

One snapshot has many rows in entity_projection_snapshots; a run target pins its snapshot ID.

09entity_projection_snapshotsentities, affordances, and provenance per snapshot
Purpose

Stable entity identity and the current semantic/geometric belief used for affordance binding and model-facing reads.

Columnsscene_snapshot_id · entity_id
type · label · affordances jsonb
components jsonb · relationships jsonb
freshness_ms · provenance jsonb
primary key (scene_snapshot_id, entity_id)
Rules

Identity must remain stable across snapshots. Observations do not assert identity; scene reduction performs association.

10attention_contractspinned inbox behavior per mission and principal
Purpose

Materialized contract that determines which events an agent notices and when a turn or wake can be created.

Columnsmission_id · principal
state_filter jsonb · wake_predicate_cel
budget jsonb · digest_version
predicate_env_version · preset_id · preset_version
created_at · updated_at
Key

Unique on (mission_id, principal). Server-injected lifecycle and owned-run themes cannot be removed.

11attention_seamspersisted delivery boundaries and digests
Purpose

Records when an inbox was drained, why it was drained, which cursor range was delivered, and what digest bytes the agent read.

Columnsid PK · mission_id · principal · seam_at
cause · cursor_start · cursor_end
digest_version · digest_ref · coalesced_counts jsonb
created_at
Links

Digest references resolve to persisted artifacts or event-derived bytes. Raw events remain in event_log.

12replay_artifactsmaterialized run reconstruction outputs
Purpose

Optional cached replay or report output for a run, while the canonical reconstruction still comes from events, authorizations, and version pins.

Columnsid PK · run_id · mission_id
event_seq_start · event_seq_end
authorization_ids jsonb · version_pins jsonb
artifact_id · content_hash · generated_at
Rule

A cache may be discarded and regenerated. It must never become the only copy of causal evidence.

13normalized_status_cachelatest robot status for reads and freshness checks
Purpose

Fast projection of the latest driver status used by Mission API reads and kernel-adjacent freshness checks.

Columnsrobot_id PK · source_seq · observed_at
heartbeat_age_ms · battery jsonb
safe_state_active · pose jsonb · faults jsonb
vendor_display jsonb
Rule

It is a cache, not authority. Driver and kernel events remain the evidence for what happened.

14artifactsdatabase-backed references to binary evidence
Purpose

Names images, masks, point clouds, audio, video, debug snapshots, and other evidence without exposing filesystem paths to the agent.

Columnsartifact_id PK · artifact_type · content_type
size_bytes · checksum · created_at
source_component_id · thread_id? · turn_id?
storage_backend · storage_key · metadata jsonb
Backends

Postgres blobs are the v0 option. The reference can later point to S3, MinIO, R2, or GCS without changing event, thread, or scene records.

Not separate v0 tables: observations and telemetry are event payloads; label_map.json and types.json are versioned ontology inputs; presets and reports are pinned artifacts or log-backed state. ClickHouse is a later analytical mirror, not the v0 source of truth.

05 / Current state

Current state

The first World Runtime slice is implemented and connected to the live Go2 operator surface. The next step is turning sensor evidence into semantic entities and relationships, then binding physical action packs to the same actions used in simulation.
